records.title: Grounds Keeper
records.description: Black Hills State University is hiring a full-time Grounds Keeper to maintain the beauty and functionality of our Rapid City campus. This position plays a vital role in supporting a safe, sustainable, and inviting environment for students, faculty, staff, and visitors. DUTIES: Maintain lawns, nurseries, trees, flowers, shrubs, and irrigation systems. Care for streets, sidewalks, and related equipment. Remove snow during winter months. Load, unload, and move furniture, equipment, materials, and supplies. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES: Strong knowledge of gardening and grounds maintenance practices. Ability to recognize and address plant diseases and insect damage. Capability to work outdoors in all weather conditions. Proficiency in following oral and written instructions. Physical ability to perform heavy lifting and manual labor. Experience operating motorized vehicles, tools, and equipment. Professional interaction with co-workers and patrons. Reliable and consistent attendance. REQUIREMENTS: Previous and demonstrated landscaping or groundskeeping experience. Occasional travel to the Spearfish campus. Ability to obtain a pesticide applicator license within the first 12-months of employment. TO APPLY: Applications for this position must be made online at http://yourfuture.sdbor.edu. Applicants must complete the online application and also attach a cover letter, resume and the names and contact information for three professional references. This position is open until filled with a first review date of August 19, 2026 at 11PM MDT. For application assistance, contact Human Resources at 605.642.6549. Questions specific to the position can be directed to Rhyse Naylor at 605.642.6147. Arrangements for accommodations required by disabilities can be made by contacting Cassie Maser at 605-642-6545 or Cassie.Maser@bhsu.edu . Employment is dependent upon a satisfactory background check.

records.title: Building Maintenance Specialist
records.description: Black Hills State University invites qualified, self-motivated candidates for a Building Maintenance Specialist for the Facilities Services Department. DUTIES: This position will be expected to maintain the heating and cooling systems of the campus and keep them in proper working order. Perform preventive, predictive, and scheduled maintenance and repairs to the HVAC and Boiler systems. RESPONSIBILITIES: Work on all campus HVAC equipment: Boilers & boiler controls Water heaters Basic energy monitoring on central and remote systems Coordinate the above HVAC work with all other facets of maintenance SUCCESSFUL CANDIDATES WILL HAVE: Experience with managing workflow processes and balancing multiple tasks simultaneously. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills. Exceptional attention to detail and accuracy. Ability to make decisions independently and to determine when consultation with supervisor is required. Ability to establish and maintain professional relationships with students, faculty, staff and the public. QUALIFICATIONS: Required: Minimum of three years of HVAC work in the field or three full years of school or a combination of both. Acquire a license within 6 months of employment. Must have working knowledge of computers, knowledge of local and national mechanical and building codes, basic knowledge of electrical controls, several years of experience in boiler controls, be able to lift heavy loads, be able to climb ladders, stairs, and scaffold, be able to work long and late hours should the need arise. COMMENTS: Periodically will be required to work at the Rapid City Campus. Typical office hours are Monday through Friday 7:00AM-3:30PM. After hours ON CALL will be required on a rotation basis. records.title: Director, Student Support Services
records.description: Black Hills State University invites applications for the position of Director of Student Support Services. This leadership position is responsible for the overall administration of the federally funded TRIO Student Support Services program in accordance with federal regulations, the approved grant proposal, and University policies and procedures. The Director provides strategic and operational leadership for the program, ensuring that its goals and objectives are effectively developed, implemented, evaluated, and documented. The position selects, trains, and supervises program staff and student employees; develops and manages the annual federal grant budget; maintains accurate participant records; and prepares grant proposals, continuation applications, Annual Performance Reports, budget reports, and other required institutional and federal reports. Join Black Hills State University and help create meaningful opportunities for students to overcome barriers, achieve their educational goals, and thrive throughout their university experience. THE SUCCESSFUL CANDIDATE: • Will be a student-centered and collaborative leader who demonstrates strong grant-management, budgeting, supervision, communication, and organizational abilities. • This individual will be committed to supporting student persistence and achievement while maintaining full compliance with federal grant requirements and University expectations. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES INCLUDE: • Coordinating, supervising, and evaluating program services and activities. • Determining student eligibility for participation in Student Support Services. • Advising a small caseload of students on course registration, FAFSA completion, study skills, academic planning, and related needs. • Providing or coordinating academic, financial, career, social, and personal support based on participant needs. • Advocating for students and ensuring equitable access and appropriate accommodations for students with disabilities and members of underrepresented populations. • Maintaining effective systems for documenting services, evaluating program performance, and measuring progress toward grant objectives. • Conducting follow-up with participants after they exit the program. • Developing strong working relationships with university administrators, faculty, and staff; vocational rehabilitation and disability services counselors; community resource providers; other postsecondary institutions; professional organizations; and government officials. • Serving as the primary liaison between program participants and campus or community partners. • Collaborating with University personnel to connect students with appropriate academic and skill-development resources. • Promoting Student Support Services to eligible students and increasing the program’s visibility both within and beyond the University. • Representing the program at University and community events, including events that support diversity and multicultural education. • Participating in administrative staff meetings and University planning initiatives. • Preparing institutional reports as directed by the Vice President for Enrollment Management. • Performing other duties as assigned by the Vice President for Enrollment Management or designee. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS: • Master’s degree • 1 to 3 years of supervisory experience as well as progressively responsible experience in higher education, student affairs, or a related field PREFERRED QUALIFICATONS: • Master’s degree in higher education, student affairs, counseling, business, or a related field. • 5-7 years of progressively responsible supervisory experience. • Previous grant writing and management experience. SALARY RANGE: • $67,000 - $72,000 depending on experience and qualifications. SPECIAL COMMENTS: • Sponsorship not available for this position. • This position is 100% grant funded. Continued employment is contingent upon grant funding. TO APPLY: Applications must be made at http://yourfuture.sdbor.edu . Please attach a cover letter, resume and the names and contact information of at least three professional references. First review for this position will begin on October 5, 2026. For application assistance, please contact Human Resources at 605.642.6549. Questions specific to the position may be directed to John Allred at john.allred@bhsu.edu . Arrangements for accommodations required by disabilities can be made by contacting Cassie Maser at 605-642-6545 or Cassie.Maser@bhsu.edu . Employment is dependent upon a satisfactory background check.

records.title: University Registrar
records.description: University Registrar Black Hills State University | Spearfish, South Dakota Black Hills State University invites applications for University Registrar. The Registrar leads the office responsible for student academic records, registration, transfer credit evaluation, academic catalogs, degree awarding, enrollment verification, and transcript services. This position protects the accuracy and confidentiality of student records while helping students, faculty, and staff navigate academic policies and processes. The University Registrar supervises office personnel; oversees registration, degree audits, and graduation processes; and works with Academic Affairs and campus partners to implement approved curriculum and improve student information systems. The Registrar also advises university leaders on academic records practices and ensures office operations comply with university, South Dakota Board of Regents, state, and federal requirements, including FERPA. ESSENTIAL DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES: a. Establish office priorities, procedures, service standards, and measures of effectiveness. b. Supervise, train, and evaluate staff; assign work and maintain coverage for critical academic deadlines. c. Develop the office budget, manage resources, document procedures, and plan for continuity of operations. d. Serve on University and Regental committees and advise campus leaders on registrar functions and the operational effects of proposed academic policies. e. Direct the creation, accuracy, security, correction, retention, and authorized release of student academic records. f. Oversee grades, academic standing actions, transcripts, enrollment and degree verifications, and other official record services. g. Interpret and implement applicable requirements under FERPA, SDBOR policies, university policies, and records retention schedules; coordinate complex questions with appropriate campus and system offices. h. Maintain controls and audit practices that protect record integrity and support accurate institutional reporting. i. Oversee registration processes, academic term setup, course section data, enrollment changes, withdrawals, and related student communications. j. Help develop and administer the academic calendar and ensure that published dates, deadlines, and procedures are accurate and consistent. k. Resolve escalated registration issues within approved policy and delegated authority. l. Coordinate implementation of approved programs, courses, prerequisites, and degree requirements in the catalog and student information system. m. Oversee production and maintenance of the academic catalog in partnership with Academic Affairs. o. Direct the recording and evaluation of transfer credit according to approved policies and articulation agreements. p. Maintain reliable degree audit rules and communicate the effects of curriculum changes to affected offices. q. Direct graduation application, degree audit, eligibility review, degree posting, diploma, and related record processes. r. Provide leadership to produce bi-annual Commencement exercises. t. Identify barriers or recurring errors in degree completion processes and recommend improvements. REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS: · Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution. · Progressively responsible experience in a college or university registrar’s office or closely related academic administration, including experience supervising personnel or leading complex operations. · Demonstrated knowledge of academic records, registration, curriculum and degree requirements, and student information systems. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS: · Master’s degree. · Experience leading multiple registrar functions at a university. · Experience with Ellucian Banner or a comparable student information system and with degree audit and catalog systems. · Experience implementing policy or system changes across multiple departments. · Knowledge of South Dakota Board of Regents policies and processes. SPECIAL COMMENTS: Sponsorship is not available for this position. TO APPLY: Applications must be made at http://yourfuture.sdbor.edu. Please attach a cover letter, resume and the names and contact information of at least three professional references. First review for this position will begin on November 15, 2026 at 11pm mountain time. For application assistance, please contact Human Resources at 605.642.6549. Questions specific to the position may be directed to John Allred at john.allred@bhsu.edu. Arrangements for accommodations required by disabilities can be made by contacting Cassie Maser at 605-642-6545 or Cassie.Maser@bhsu.edu. Employment is dependent upon a satisfactory background check.

records.title: Graduate Enrollment Counselor
records.description: Black Hills State University seeks a motivated, organized, and dynamic individual to serve as the Graduate Enrollment Counselor. This position manages the full graduate student enrollment funnel from initial prospective inquiry through application file review, acceptance decisions, and census enrollment. Serving as the primary admissions liaison across graduate academic departments, the counselor evaluates applicant credentials, facilitates timely file review workflows with graduate program coordinators, and guides candidates through the admission and onboarding processes. In addition, the counselor supports graduate recruitment and marketing initiatives by researching area employer tuition benefits and workforce incentives, maintaining program marketing flyers and collateral, and updating graduate web content. This position requires strong attention to detail, excellent communication skills, initiative, flexibility, and the ability to work effectively with faculty, staff, corporate partners, and adult learners. This is a 12-month, benefit-eligible position.    RESPONSIBILITIES:  • Manage and coordinate the full graduate enrollment funnel from prospective student inquiry through application completion, evaluation, formal admission, and census enrollment.  • Audit domestic and international application portfolios for completeness, evaluate transcripts, and verify prerequisite coursework against program standards.  • Facilitate and monitor application review workflows across academic department chairs and graduate program coordinators to ensure timely review and rapid decision turnaround. • Formally issue admissions decisions (admit, provisional admit, deferral, denial) and official offer letters in alignment with Graduate Studies policies.  • Execute proactive yield initiatives to convert admitted students into enrolled cohorts, assisting with intent-to-enroll confirmations, registration obstacle resolution, and onboarding to reduce melt.  • Deliver personalized admissions advising to prospective adult, post-traditional, and online learners via telephone, email, and virtual appointments regarding program curricula, delivery formats, and admissions pathways.  • Research regional employers, school districts, healthcare networks, and public agencies to identify tuition assistance and reimbursement policies, establishing contacts to build workforce enrollment pipelines.  • Review, update, and maintain print and digital promotional collateral, including program flyers, one-page informational sheets, brochures, and graduate admissions web pages in collaboration with University Marketing and Communications.  • Administer the recruitment CRM and Student Information System (SIS) to maintain accurate applicant records, configure communication sequences, monitor conversion metrics across each funnel stage, and generate regular pipeline reports for academic leadership.  • Serve as an admissions liaison to campus partner offices, including Financial Aid, the Registrar, Veteran Affairs, and academic advising units, to support student onboarding.  • Represent Graduate Studies at regional career fairs, community gatherings, campus events, and university committee meetings.  • Occasional evening and/or weekend work will be required for recruitment events, webinars, and campus milestone activities.  • Demonstrated written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present effectively to groups and convey academic policies clearly.  • Strong organizational, analytical, and time management skills with the ability to manage multiple competing deadlines independently.  • Demonstrated proficiency with CRM platforms, student information systems, or standard office productivity software.  • Ability to work effectively and collaboratively with diverse populations, including adult learners, faculty, and external community partners.  • Experience researching corporate tuition assistance policies and conducting B2B or employer outreach.  • Experience navigating decentralized faculty review processes within a college or university setting.   MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:  • A bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution.  • Two years of professional experience in higher education admissions, academic advising, student services, corporate recruiting, or marketing.    PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:  • Master’s degree from an accredited institution in higher education administration, counseling, business, communications, or a related field.  • Demonstrated experience designing and updating print and digital promotional materials (e.g., flyers, one-pagers, brochures) using design software.  • Familiarity with Ellucian software and web content management software.  • Direct experience in graduate admissions, academic credential evaluation, or full lifecycle enrollment management.    SPECIAL COMMENTS: • Sponsorship is not available for this position.   TO APPLY: Applications must be made online at https://yourfuture.sdbor.edu . Please attach a cover letter, resume, and names/contact information of at least three professional references. This position is open until filled with a first review date of November 5, 2026 at 11PM MDT. For application assistance, contact Human Resources at 605.642.6549. Questions specific to the position may be directed to Rich Loose at Rich.Loose@bhsu.edu. Arrangements for accommodations required by disabilities can be made by contacting Cassie Maser at 605-642-6545 or Cassie.Maser@bhsu.edu . Employment is dependent upon a satisfactory background check.
